$comment: Published operator image releases that are known to be defective. A release tag is immutable and cannot be withdrawn, so this file is where a consumer — and the upgrade-path acceptance stage — can read that one should not be deployed. usableAsUpgradeBaseline says something narrower: whether the release can still migrate a fresh database into a faithful prior state, which is all the acceptance stage asks of it. State the verified scope of a defect, not the reported one; a reason that overstates its blast radius is how a release gets written off for the wrong reason.

knownBad.reason: Absorbing availability into operations (#4281) moved the migration ledger identity of the absorbed migrations. Managed deployments upgrading onto this release failed with: relation "allocation_audit_log" already exists.
knownBad.scope: The failure is specific to the source-free loadModuleBundleSource(packageName) resolution a downstream derivative uses, which has no migration plan to carry the retired source's identity. It does NOT reproduce through the published image's own run-generated-migrations.mjs: migrating a real 0.5.0 database (the last pre-absorption release) with this image applies 2, skips 31, boots, and re-runs as a no-op.
knownBad.baselineNote: Verified, not assumed: it migrates a fresh database correctly and a 0.5.0 database upgrades onto it cleanly, so the prior state it produces is faithful.
